source.title: Additive Combinatorics: A Menu of Research Problems

accepted.question_text: For finite abelian groups written additively, and for an m-element subset A of a group G, determine the maximum possible cardinality of the standard sumset variants formed from A, including hA, [0,s]A, the signed variants h±A and [0,s]±A, the restricted variants ĥA and [0,s]Â, and the restricted signed variants ĥ±A and [0,s]̂±A. Equivalently, determine the values of the maximum-size functions ν(G,m,h), ν(G,m,[0,s]), ν±(G,m,h), ν±(G,m,[0,s]), ν̂(G,m,h), ν̂(G,m,[0,s]), ν̂±(G,m,h), and ν̂±(G,m,[0,s]), and characterize extremal subsets when possible.
accepted.context_brief: Maximum sumset size in finite abelian groups

evidence.quote:
Entrees. Each chapter in this main part of the book discusses a particular fam ily of
open questions in additive combinatorics. At the present time, thes e questions are about
– maximum sumset size,
– spanning sets,
– Sidon sets,
– minimum sumset size,
– critical numbers,
– zero-sum-free sets, and
– sum-free sets.

Within most sub sections, we
investigate both direct questions (e.g. what is the maximum size of a set with the required
sumset property) and inverse questions (how can we characterize all subsets that achieve
this maximum size).

accepted.question_text: For a finite abelian group G, determine the minimum size of a subset A needed so that A spans G under each of the standard sumset operations: hA = G, [0,s]A = G, ⟨A⟩ = G, h±A = G, [0,s]±A = G, restricted ĥA = G, restricted [0,s]Â = G, ΣA = G, restricted signed ĥ±A = G, restricted signed [0,s]̂±A = G, and Σ±A = G. Equivalently, determine the spanning-set threshold functions φ, φ±, φ̂, and φ̂± and characterize extremal spanning sets where possible.
